bull_bear.body: Prioritizing organic growth in Acemoney and RVL; cash balance of INR80cr provides flexibility for strategic acquisitions; no dividend or buyback mentioned; Acemoney acquisition model (high ROI) as template for future M&A
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Sluggish BFSI demand (MFI/personal loan); UPI adoption in Tier 4/5; RVL breakeven delay; high fixed cost structure limiting margin expansion without revenue growth; regulatory scrutiny on fintech data security (mitigated by PCI DSS)
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident and strategic; focused on long-term secular trends (cash-in-circulation, rural digitization); transparent about RVL losses and timeline; optimistic on Acemoney scalability; committed to margin recovery
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Acemoney's transaction-based revenue model (not device sales) creates sticky, scalable unit economics; RVL's 50-50 air/road split leverages existing cash logistics network without new capex; cash loss rates near zero due to ex-service culture, not just tech
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Nationwide physical network of 14,844 PIN codes, 9,162 operational locations and 77,521 customer touchpoints spanning urban, semi-urban and rural India
- Integrated solutions combining cash logistics, processing, cash management, fintech and valuable logistics in a single end-to-end portfolio
- Falling customer concentration: top 10 clients contributed 70% of revenue in FY 2026 versus 80% in FY 2024, and top 5 clients 49% versus 58%
- Technology enablement through AWS cloud migration of the ERP environment, API integration with client ERP systems and real-time transaction visibility
- Enduring customer relationships built on consistent execution and service excellence, with a marquee client base of leading banks, NBFCs, retail, e-commerce and government institutions
- Compliance-led operations backed by standardised SOPs, a risk management framework and a skilled workforce of 2,641 employees
- Regulated operating environment: vehicles used for cash logistics operations are governed by RBI/MHA guidelines, favouring organised providers
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Privacy and data security — As a cash management service company the business involves sensitive financial data, and any disruption or leakage would endanger the company; timely and secure transmission of data is critical to operations. Mitigated through a cybersecurity policy and data storage and transmission facilities with 100% backups. Flagged with negative financial implications.
- Labour management and workforce dependence — Poor labour management is identified as a significant risk that can lead to service disruptions and adverse impact on the Company's reputation, with workforce expectations rising over time. Mitigation is continuous interaction with the workforce and swift grievance redressal. Flagged with negative financial implications.
- Carbon emissions and vehicle-fleet regulation — Stricter government regulation to mitigate climate change and reduce carbon emissions exposes the company to legal issues and penalties. The nature of vehicles used for cash logistics operations is regulated by RBI/MHA guidelines; vehicles in Delhi and NCR have been switched to CNG from petrol/diesel, with periodic pollution control checks and regular servicing. Flagged with negative financial implications.
- Human rights compliance across the operating footprint — Violation of human rights in any location where the company has business interest would result in agitations and loss of productivity. The company commits to prohibition of child labour, prohibition of forced and compulsory labour and freedom of association, with periodic human rights training and open field-team feedback channels. Flagged with negative financial implications.
- Business ethics, anti-money-laundering and regulatory conduct — Operating in the financial industry, adherence to anti-corruption, anti-money laundering, insider trading, fair taxation and auditing practices is key to operations; non-adherence would lead to legal fines. Identified as a material responsible-business-conduct issue.
- Loss-making Valuable Logistics business — Continued losses in the Valuable Logistics business, alongside higher operating expenses, held back profitability during the year even though revenue was broadly stable; the business remains in a consolidation phase with the payoff from prior-year efforts still pending.
- Fintech subsidiary performance and policy dependence — The decline in consolidated profitability was primarily attributable to the fintech subsidiary Aceware Fintech Services Private Limited, whose performance was impacted by the discontinuation of the RBI Payment Infrastructure Development Fund (PIDF) subsidy scheme and increased manpower — a direct dependence of subsidiary economics on a regulator-run subsidy scheme.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: Radiant Cash Management Services Limited operates an end-to-end portfolio spanning cash logistics, cash management and digital financial services, delivered through an integrated business portfolio of Retail Cash Management, Cash Processing, Network Currency Management, Cash Van Operations, Valuable Logistics and Fintech. It serves leading banks, NBFCs, retail and e-commerce customers and government institutions, with deep physical presence across urban, semi-urban and rural India supported by proprietary applications, API integrations and cloud infrastructure. Its cash logistics vehicles operate under RBI/MHA guidelines, and the group also runs a fintech subsidiary offering merchant ecosystem, Business Correspondent and digital banking access services.
business.title: What they do

business.body:
- **Cash logistics and cash management:** Retail Cash Management, Cash Processing, Network Currency Management, Cash Van Operations
- **Valuable Logistics:** Valuable Logistics
- **Fintech:** Merchant ecosystem, Business Correspondent services, Digital banking access
- **Customer-facing technology platforms:** Radmus mobile application, Radiant Sandesh mobile application, Client View Portal, CPIN / OTP Authentication, QR-enabled Cash Collection
business.title: Products & brands

business.body:
- Aceware Fintech Services Private Limited — subsidiary: Fintech subsidiary, 58.21% of shares held by the listed entity; acquired 01/12/2023. Does not participate in the Business Responsibility initiatives of the listed entity. Related-party arrangements run up to March 31, 2027 (board approval 23rd May, 2025) and cover commission for onboarding merchants and Business Correspondent (BC) agents, reimbursement of remuneration for personnel on deputation, inter-corporate loan and corporate guarantee.
- Acemoney Payment Solutions Private Limited — subsidiary: Named in Form AOC-1 as a subsidiary that was liquidated or ceased during the year.
- Radiant Protection Force Private Limited — related party: Related party under significant influence; material arm's-length contracts up to March 31, 2026 (board approval 18th February, 2023; shareholder approval by postal ballot dated March 23, 2023 covering FY 2023-24 to FY 2025-26) for services of gunmen, guards and drivers, lease rentals of vehicles, generators and cash vans, fleet operating and service charges, cash van running and maintenance expenses including reimbursement of expenses, lease rent for office premises, and an inter-corporate loan.

outlook.body: Rural fintech penetration (50%+ merchant outlets still cash-only); jewelry logistics market (1.35L jewelers, only 25K serviced); direct B2B cash services to unbanked retail chains; cross-selling Insta Credit to Acemoney merchants
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Integrated solutions: build an end-to-end portfolio combining cash logistics, cash processing, cash management, fintech and valuable logistics rather than a single service line
- Nationwide reach: maintain deep physical presence across urban, semi-urban and rural India, with a strong network penetrating Tier II and Tier III markets
- Technology enablement: digital platforms, cloud infrastructure, automation and customer visibility, executed in FY 2025-26 through migration of the ERP environment to AWS Cloud, API integration with client ERP systems, the Client View Portal, Radmus and Radiant Sandesh mobile applications and QR/CPIN-OTP enabled cash collection
- Financial inclusion: extend the merchant ecosystem, Business Correspondent services and digital banking access to enable last-mile banking
- Sustainable growth through diversified revenues, stronger customer relationships and scalable operations
- Reduce revenue dependence on a few customers by broadening the client base; top 5 client share fell from 58% in FY 2024 to 49% in FY 2026 and top 10 from 80% to 70%
- Consolidate the loss-making Valuable Logistics business so that prior-year efforts translate into results
- Strengthen cybersecurity and software engineering discipline through CERT-In certified VAPT, SonarQube and Bitbucket Pipelines
- Expand and upskill the workforce, with leadership inductions, leadership development programmes and structured learning to support the next phase of growth
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The annual report describes no physical plant or capacity expansion project. Radiant's expansion narrative for FY 2025-26 is asset-light and technology- and footprint-led: it migrated its ERP environment to AWS Cloud to strengthen scalability, business continuity and operational resilience, built out customer-facing technology through API integration with client ERP systems, the Client View Portal, the Radmus and Radiant Sandesh mobile applications, CPIN/OTP authentication and QR-enabled cash collection, and strengthened secure operations through CERT-In certified Vulnerability Assessment and Penetration Testing and modern software engineering tooling (SonarQube, Bitbucket Pipelines). Management states these investments position the company to support future growth with greater agility and provide scalable digital infrastructure. On the people side, the company expanded its workforce to 2,641 employees nationwide to support business expansion, operational requirements and evolving customer expectations, adding 8 leadership inductions and running 15+ training programmes. No commissioning dates, project names or capex quantum for any expansion project are disclosed in this bundle; the only rupee capital figure disclosed is the capital commitments note.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Hybrid payments economy: cash and digital transactions coexist, with currency in circulation at an all-time high of Rs 41.6 trillion in FY 2026 while UPI transaction value rose to Rs 314 trillion, creating sustained demand for secure cash logistics and digitally connected operations
- Financial inclusion: expanding banking access and merchant digitisation are creating greater demand for organised cash management and assisted banking services
- Economic formalisation: greater regulatory compliance, organised retail expansion and increasing digital adoption continue to support organised cash logistics providers
- Growing outsourcing: banks and enterprises are increasingly entrusting treasury, cash handling and secure logistics to specialised service providers
- Regional growth: rising economic activity in Tier II and Tier III markets continues to support demand for reliable last-mile cash logistics
- Technology-led operations: automation, real-time visibility and intelligent digital systems are enhancing efficiency, security and service quality across the cash management value chain
- Macro backdrop: India's real GDP expanded 7.7% in FY 2025-26 with inflation moderating to 3.48%, and GDP is projected to grow 6.6% in FY 2027 on sustained capital investment, improving credit offtake and resilient domestic consumption
- Near-term profitability drag: revenue was broadly stable but profitability was hit by higher operating expenses and continued losses in the Valuable Logistics business, which management says is in its consolidation phase with prior-year efforts expected to materialise in the current financial year
- Consolidated profitability decline attributed to the fintech subsidiary Aceware Fintech Services Private Limited, whose performance was impacted by the discontinuation of the RBI Payment Infrastructure Development Fund (PIDF) subsidy scheme and increased manpower
